verifications.claim: Artemis II is a 10-day crewed mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "epic 10-day odyssey" (R1); "10 days in space" (R2); "9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes" but described as 10-day (R3); "10 days in space" (R4); "10-day mission" (R5); "10 days later" (R6); "10-day journey" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly describe Artemis II as a 10-day crewed mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to launch no earlier than April 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "targeting a launch in April 2026" (R3); "scheduled to lift off from Launch Pad 39B at Kennedy Space Center in Florida as soon as April 1" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm the schedule was delayed to no earlier than April 2026.

verifications.claim: Per recent April 1, 2026 updates, Artemis II launched on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Artemis II heads to the moon: Four astronauts... after successfully conducting the translunar injection burn" dated 2026/04/01 (R2); "Launch date April 1, 2026, 22:35:12 UTC" (R3); "Artemis II has successfully launched! ... at 6:35 p.m. ET" on April 1 (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Post-launch sources dated around April 1, 2026, confirm the launch occurred on that date.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "four astronauts onboard the Orion spacecraft" for tests (R1); "first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft" (R3); "test the systems onboard the Orion spacecraft" (R4); "test Orion’s systems" (R5)

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first human return to the moon's vicinity since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first time astronauts return to the vicinity of the moon in more than 50 years" (R2); "first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972" (R3); "first time in nearly 54 years, humans are on their way to the moon" since Apollo 17 (R4); "first humans back to the Moon in over 50 years" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state it as the first since Apollo 17 in 1972.

verifications.claim: SLS places the crew in an initial high-Earth orbit for testing during Artemis II launch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "after the launch and separation from the immense Space Launch System rocket, the crew will spend their first day in space positioning Orion in a high Earth orbit" (R1); "high Earth orbit... for testing" after SLS (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe SLS placing crew into high Earth orbit for initial testing.

verifications.claim: On Day 1 of Artemis II, Orion performs a manual, human-piloted proximity operations test (Proximity Operations Demonstration).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first day in space positioning Orion in a high Earth orbit" implying tests (R1); "proximity operations demonstration using the spent Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS)" on flight day 1 (R3); "proximity operations, or 'prox ops'" on day 1 (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm proximity operations demo on day 1, manually piloted.

verifications.claim: On Days 2–4 of Artemis II, the service module fires for a translunar injection (TLI).
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "day two, Orion will perform its “translunar injection burn,” firing its main engine" (R1); "flight day 2... TLI burn using the ESM's AJ10 main engine" (R3); "translunar injection burn" day 2 (R5); TLI after day 1 (R6,R7)
verifications.reasoning: TLI specifically on day 2 via service module; days 2-4 include corrections, but claim specifies TLI on 2-4, slightly broader.

verifications.claim: On Days 2–4 of Artemis II, the translunar injection places the craft on a figure-eight trajectory toward the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "there-and-back-again voyage will trace out a figure-eight-like path" after TLI (R1); "free-return trajectory" after TLI day 2 (R3); "figure-eight flight path to the moon" days 2-4 (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources link TLI to figure-eight/free-return trajectory around days 2-4.

verifications.claim: On Days 5–6 of Artemis II, the crew travels roughly 4,600 miles beyond the lunar far side.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "day six will take... to the far side" (R1); "Closest approach... 4,067 mi" on day 6 (R3); "closest approach to the Moon at about 6,545 kilometers (4,067 miles)" days 5-6 (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm travel beyond lunar far side days 5-6 at ~4,067 miles; 4,600 is roughly approximate.

verifications.claim: On Days 5–6 of Artemis II, the crew uses the lunar far side for a gravity-assisted return.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "pulled back earthward by our planet’s gravity" after lunar far side (R1); "free-return trajectory... looping around the far side" (R3); "free-return trajectory" using moon's gravity (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Free-return uses lunar gravity assist from far side on days 5-6.

verifications.claim: On Days 5–6 of Artemis II, the crew takes photos of the lunar far side.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "taking photos of the moon, which at closest approach... They’ll also try to capture new images of “Earthrise" day six (R1); "photographed... lunar surface" during flyby day 6 (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify photos of lunar far side on days 5-6.

verifications.claim: On Days 7–9 of Artemis II, the crew transits back to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "after their lunar encounter, the astronauts will spend the next few days prepping for their homecoming" (R1); "Return flight" days 7-9 (R3); "beginning the return trip back to Earth" after day 6 (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe return transit on days 7-9.

verifications.claim: On Day 10 of Artemis II, the crew module separates from the service module.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "day 10. Then the smaller crew module will detach from the rest of Orion" (R1); "crew module separates from the ESM before reentry day 10" (R3); "Orion’s crew module will separate from the service module" day 10 (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of separation on day 10.

verifications.claim: On Day 10 of Artemis II, the crew module enters the atmosphere at 3,000∘F.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "atmospheric reentry, which will heat the spacecraft’s exterior to a blistering 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit (1,650 degrees Celsius) on day 10" (R1); "temperatures of about 1,650 degrees Celsius (3,000 degrees Fahrenheit)" day 10 (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Exact temperature match for reentry on day 10.

verifications.claim: On Day 10 of Artemis II, the crew module lands in the Pacific Ocean with a parachute-assisted splashdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "parachutes will deploy to slow their descent for a tranquil... plunge to splashdown in the Pacific Ocean" day 10 (R1); "splashdown... Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego" (R3); "splash down into the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego" day 10 (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm parachute splashdown in Pacific on day 10.
